steps.tx: A **tibial shaft fracture** is the most frequent long bone fracture encountered in orthopaedic trauma centers. Because the entire anteromedial surface of the tibia is subcutaneous and devoid of muscular coverage, it has the highest propensity for open fracture among all long bones. High-energy motor vehicle crashes and pedestrian strikes generate severe soft tissue stripping and devascularization.
steps.say: The tibia is the most frequently broken long bone. Because its entire shin border lies directly beneath the skin without muscular padding, it has the highest rate of open fractures. High-speed collisions crush the skin and strip periosteum, jeopardizing bone healing.

vis.title: Tibial Anatomy and Vulnerability
rows: High rate of open fractures and skin necrosis
Enters upper third via posterior cortex
Distal third relies on tenuous periosteal arcade
Extreme vulnerability to acute compartment syndrome

steps.tx: The **Gustilo-Anderson classification** categorizes open tibial fractures to guide antibiotic selection and surgical debridement. Type I features a clean puncture wound smaller than one centimeter. Type II has a laceration between one and ten centimeters without extensive soft tissue damage. Type III involves extensive soft tissue trauma, subdivided into IIIa (adequate periosteal coverage), IIIb (periosteal stripping requiring flap coverage), and IIIc (arterial injury requiring repair).
steps.say: Gustilo and Anderson classify open fractures into three tiers. Type one is under one centimeter. Type two is one to ten centimeters without extensive soft tissue crushing. Type three has severe soft tissue damage, split into three A with adequate coverage, three B requiring plastic flap coverage, and three C with vascular damage requiring arterial repair.

vis.title: Gustilo-Anderson Open Fracture Classification
rows: Any open wound with vascular injury

steps.tx: The most urgent complication is **compartment syndrome** of the leg, arising within twenty-four hours from osseous haemorrhage and muscle oedema enclosed by non-compliant fascial envelopes. Unremitting pain out of proportion to injury exacerbated by passive toe extension is the earliest sensitive warning. Intracompartmental pressure within thirty millimeters of mercury of diastolic blood pressure mandates emergent four-compartment fasciotomy.
steps.say: Acute compartment syndrome is the most urgent threat. The four tight fascial envelopes in the leg cannot stretch when bleeding starts. Severe pain provoked by passive stretching of the toes is the earliest warning. If compartment pressure rises to within thirty millimeters of diastolic blood pressure, perform emergency four-compartment fasciotomy.

left.title: Early Warning Signs
points: Pain out of proportion to injury
Pain on passive toe flexion and extension

right.title: Late Catastrophic Signs
points: Loss of distal dorsalis pedis pulse

steps.tx: Closed, low-energy fractures with minimal shortening may be managed with **functional bracing** using a Sarmiento patellar-tendon-bearing cast. Initiated after initial swelling subsides at two to four weeks, the brace loads the patellar tendon, tibial flares, and hydrostatic muscle envelope. Permitting controlled cyclical axial micromotion stimulates robust external bridging callus while restoring knee and ankle mobility.
steps.say: For closed, stable fractures with under five degrees of angulation, use a Sarmiento patellar tendon bearing cast after initial swelling settles. The cast unloads the fracture by transferring weight through the patellar tendon and calf muscles, allowing early walking that accelerates callus formation.

right.title: Sarmiento Bracing Protocol
points: Long leg cast for first 2 to 3 weeks

steps.tx: The surgical gold standard for unstable, displaced, or open fractures is **intramedullary nailing** using a reamed interlocking nail. A transpatellar or infrapatellar tendon approach allows insertion of an unreamed or reamed nail with proximal and distal locking screws. Intramedullary fixation provides load-sharing biomechanics, protects the periosteal blood supply, and achieves union rates exceeding ninety-five percent.
steps.say: Reamed interlocking intramedullary nailing is the definitive surgical gold standard. The nail acts as an internal splint that shares load, preserves periosteal blood flow, and controls length and rotation. Patients can bear weight immediately, achieving union in over ninety-five percent of cases.

vis.title: Surgical Fixation Modalities
rows: Gustilo IIIb/IIIc, severe contaminated open break

quiz.q: Which Gustilo-Anderson category requires a muscle flap transfer due to extensive periosteal stripping and soft tissue defect?
quiz.explain: Gustilo Type IIIb fractures exhibit extensive soft tissue loss with periosteal stripping and bone exposure, requiring local or free flap coverage.

quiz.q: What difference between diastolic blood pressure and compartment pressure (delta P) indicates need for fasciotomy?
quiz.explain: A delta P (diastolic blood pressure minus intracompartmental pressure) of 30 mmHg or less indicates critical tissue ischaemia and mandates urgent fasciotomy.
